description: Standex International Corporation, through it subsidiaries, engages in the manufacture and sale of products and services for commercial and industrial markets in the United States and internationally.
description_full: Standex International Corporation, through it subsidiaries, engages in the manufacture and sale of products and services for commercial and industrial markets in the United States and internationally. It operates through Electronics, Aerospace & Defense, Scientific, Engraving & Hydraulics segments. The company offers reed relays, fluid level, proximity, motion, flow, HVAC condensate, custom electronic and current sensors, instrument transformers, wound transformers, bushings, inductors, current sense and planar transformer technology, value added assemblies, mechanical packaging applications under the Standex Electronics, Standex-Meder Electronics, Renco Electronics, Northlake Engineering, Agile Magnetics, Sensor Solutions, Standex Electronics Japan, Minntronix, Nascentechnology, Sanyu, Amran Instruments, and Narayan Powertech brands. It also provides mold texturizing, slush molding tools, project management and design services, roll engraving, hygiene product tooling, low observation vents for stealth aircraft, and process machinery services under the Mold Tech, Piazza Rosa, World Client Services, Tenibac-Graphion, GS Engineering, and Innovent and Custom Hoists brands. In addition, it provides specialty temperature-controlled equipment for medical, scientific, pharmaceutical, biotech, and industrial markets under the American BioTech Supply, Lab Research Products, Corepoint, Cryosafe, CryoGuard, and Custom Biogenic Systems brands; and net and near net formed single-source customized solutions for the aviation, aerospace, defense, energy, industrial, medical, marine, oil and gas, and manned and unmanned space markets under the Spincraft and McStarlite brands. Further, it offers refrigerated, heated, display cases, single and double acting telescopic, and piston rod hydraulic cylinders under the Federal and Custom Hoist brands. The company was founded in 1955 and is headquartered in Salem, New Hampshire.

financial_summary: Standex International Corporati is a mid-cap industrials business with a $2.8B market cap on $892M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +6% over the past three years and +2% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 13% against a 9% cost of capital, a 4-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 35%.

The business throws off $64M in free cash flow — roughly 7 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.86× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.5× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 6.3×.

Shareholder yield is only 0.7%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 2.0× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 22% operating margin runs 13pp above the Industrials median (9%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 1.97x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+17.8% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.01 across 544 companies in the universe; the top four hold 9% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 27% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 31% over the last three months.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 37% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 40% and a beta of 0.95, it moves roughly with the market.
About $36.2M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 51% in the 2020 crash, 27% in the 2022 bear market and 73% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $211 (margin of safety -8%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 41%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $133 to $340 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Industrials peers: P/FCF 42.9 vs 22.3 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 2% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 2.3% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 5.9% (vs the 8% bar).
The 5 covering analysts target $332 on average, 46% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 13% earns above the cost of capital of 8.7%, but the 4pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.36).
It runs a 35% gross margin and converts 7% of revenue into free cash flow.
ROE of 14% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.1x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 9pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 2.7% of revenue on R&D and 0.7% on stock compensation.
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 1.5x net debt to EBITDA ($178.7M of cash against $518.0M of debt), with interest covered 6.3x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 4.3, in the safe zone).
Goodwill makes up 37% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 6.4% over 3 years, 6.3% over 5 years and 1.7% over 10 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 0.8% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Capex runs only 0.7x depreciation (2.8% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 3.0% on average.
Analysts expect 20.3% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own a modest 1.8%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insider trading is two-way: 2 purchases and 8 sales over the past year, net $5.2M sold.
Shareholder yield is a modest 0.7% (0.2% in buybacks and 0.6% in dividends).
It has paid a dividend for 39 consecutive years, raising it 7.2% a year over the last five.
people: With about 4,100 employees, each generates about $217K of revenue, 0.6x the Industrials median.
That works out to $16K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.6M (8x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (1/10, lower is better).
